status.summary: Top flyweight contender coming off a title loss. Challenged Joshua Van at UFC 328 (May 9, 2026), won the early grappling exchanges (10:38 of control, 8 takedowns) but was dropped late in round 2 and stopped by punches at 1:32 of round 5; he protested the stoppage. Before that he became the first man to stop Brandon Moreno (TKO from back control, UFC 323, Dec 6, 2025). UFC record 8-2. No booking found as of early Nov 2026.

style.summary: A Japanese grappler who chains takedown attempts until one lands, then holds top position, takes the back and hunts chokes, armbars and ground strikes. He has controlled even elite strikers for long stretches, but his stand-up is low-output and hittable, and both UFC losses came when strikers out-landed him standing.

moves.notes: Groups follow his target split in fighters.json: decayed significant attempts 86% head, 6% body, 8% legs (career 85/6/9); landed 80% head, 7% body, 13% legs. 23% of decayed attempts (30% career) are ground strikes, which the engine's ground states cover, so standing weights only describe his range work. No source breaks down his stand-up by technique, so the head group is a generic jab-cross set-up for takedowns, and the body and leg splits are judgments. Knees and elbows are low because clinch strikes are only 4% of attempts. Sources: data/derived/fighters.json, data/raw ufcstats per-fight stats.

engine_notes.note: Spends 54% of his UFC fight time in control (career; 53% decayed) vs about 19% for the flyweight prior, with 3.57 takedowns per 15 min at 44%.

At UFC 328 he won round 1 with four takedowns and round 4 with ground control and submission hunting, yet lost by round-5 TKO after being hurt by a body shot: control does not protect him from late damage.
Both UFC losses went to strikers who out-landed him heavily (Royval 124-42; Van 131-55) despite his control time (12:13 and 10:38).
